_about: Sylvester's exercise library: what each exercise trains (pattern, family and level for progressions, purposes), what it needs (equipment) and what it loads (stresses, matched against a person's limits). Conditions are general guidance with sources; the Coach turns them into each person's own limits. See coach/library.py and coach/knowledge/exercise_library.md.

patterns.squat: Knee- and hip-bend on two legs (squats, sit-to-stand, wall sit).
patterns.lunge: Single-leg knee-dominant: split squats, lunges, step-ups, single-leg squats.
patterns.hinge: Hip-dominant: bridges, hip thrusts, deadlifts, swings, hamstring work.
patterns.push_h: Horizontal push: push-ups, bench and floor presses, chest presses, dips.
patterns.push_v: Vertical push: overhead and landmine presses, pike push-ups.
patterns.pull_h: Horizontal pull: rows, inverted rows, pull-aparts, face pulls.
patterns.pull_v: Vertical pull: pull-ups, chin-ups, pulldowns, hangs.
patterns.carry: Loaded walking: farmer, suitcase, front-rack, overhead, rucking, sled.
patterns.core_ext: Anti-extension: resisting the low back arching (dead bug, planks, roll-outs).
patterns.core_rot: Anti-rotation: resisting twisting (Pallof press, bird dog, renegade row).
patterns.core_lat: Anti-lateral flexion: resisting side-bending (side planks, Copenhagen planks).
patterns.core_flex: Trunk flexion: crunches, sit-ups, leg raises. Listed so limits can exclude them.
patterns.rotation: Controlled or powerful rotation: chops, lifts, rotational throws.
patterns.power: Fast, explosive work: jumps, throws, slams, push press.
patterns.locomotion: Crawling and floor-based movement: bear crawl, get-ups, getting down and up.
patterns.shoulder: Shoulder health and size: raises, rotator cuff, scapular work.
patterns.lower_acc: Lower-body accessories: calves, shins, adductors, glute medius, knee and tendon work.
patterns.grip: Grip and forearm, wrist and elbow health.
patterns.mobility: Range of motion and joint control.

power.label: Power
power.dose: 3–5 × 3–5 fast reps, full rest, stop before speed drops

balance.label: Balance
balance.dose: 2–3 × 20–40 s per side, near a support

rehab.label: Rehab and joint health
rehab.dose: 2–3 × 10–20 slow, pain ≤ 3/10 that settles by the next morning

bone.label: Bone loading
bone.dose: Heavy-ish (RPE 7–8) weight-bearing lifts and, where safe, impact, 2–3×/week

bp.label: Blood pressure
bp.dose: Isometric: 4 × 2 min at a hard-but-steady effort, 2 min rest, 3×/week; breathe throughout

glucose.label: Blood sugar
glucose.dose: Big muscles, whole-body sessions; walk 10–15 min after meals

athletic.label: Real-life strength
athletic.dose: Carries, get-ups, single-leg and rotational work, 2–3 × moderate

stresses.spine_axial: Compression down the spine: bar on the back, heavy overhead or heavy carries.
stresses.spine_flex_loaded: Bending the spine forward under load or many times (sit-ups, crunches, rounded lifting).
stresses.spine_flex_end: End-range forward bending without load (child's pose, toe touches).
stresses.spine_ext_end: End-range back arching (press-ups, supermans, back extensions past neutral).
stresses.spine_rot_loaded: Twisting the spine under load or fast (Russian twists, rotational throws).
stresses.spine_shear: Long-lever bent-over positions that load the low back (bent-over rows, RDLs, good mornings).
stresses.floor_lift: Lifting a load from the floor.
stresses.knee_deep: Loaded deep knee bend (deep squats, pistols, full lunges).
stresses.knee_open: Open-chain knee extension under load (leg extension).
stresses.plantar: High load through the foot and calf (calf raises, long walks, skipping).
stresses.wrist_ext: Bodyweight on the hands with the wrist bent back (push-ups, planks, crawls).
stresses.grip_heavy: Heavy or long gripping (carries, hangs, deadlifts).
stresses.shoulder_end: Loaded shoulder end range (dips, deep flyes, deficit push-ups).
stresses.hanging: Hanging the body from the arms.
stresses.high_pressure: Big pressure spikes in the chest, belly and blood vessels: heavy or near-maximal efforts, hard bracing.
stresses.floor_transition: Getting down to and up from the floor.
stresses.balance: Single-leg or unstable: a fall risk.
stresses.ballistic: Fast or explosive: swings, throws, jumps.
stresses.neck: Load through the neck or head.

lumbar_disc.label: Lumbar disc problem (herniation, degeneration, sciatica)
lumbar_disc.notes: Keep the spine near neutral under load; build trunk endurance (McGill's curl-up, side plank, bird dog). If an exercise sends symptoms further down the leg, stop it that day. Loaded flexion's risk is clearest in lab studies; clinical trials show most exercise types help back pain about equally, so choose what the person tolerates and enjoys.

lumbar_stenosis.label: Lumbar spinal stenosis
lumbar_stenosis.notes: Back arching and long standing narrow the canal; slightly flexed positions (cycling, incline walking) are usually better tolerated.

hypertension.label: High blood pressure
hypertension.notes: Breathe out on every effort; never hold the breath across reps; stop 2–3 reps short of failure; no maximal attempts. Isometric training (wall sit, handgrip) lowered resting BP the most in the largest meta-analysis (−8/−4 mmHg); dynamic resistance and aerobic work help too. Untreated very high readings (≥ 160/100) need a doctor first.

heart.label: Heart condition
heart.notes: Needs a doctor's or cardiac-rehab clearance and their limits (heart rate, RPE) before training.

osteoporosis.label: Osteoporosis or low bone density
osteoporosis.notes: Progressive resistance and balance training are the backbone; avoid forward bending and twisting of the spine, especially under load. Supervised heavy training and impact (LIFTMOR) improved bone in trials but needs supervision; after a vertebral fracture, the treating clinician sets the limits.

knee_oa.label: Knee osteoarthritis
knee_oa.notes: Strengthening clearly helps; closed-chain work (squats, step-ups) may help pain slightly more than open-chain in the short term. Work in a pain-tolerable range (≤ 3/10, settled by the next morning).

patellofemoral.label: Kneecap pain (patellofemoral)
patellofemoral.notes: Open- and closed-chain programmes give similar long-term results; combine hip and knee strengthening and adjust depth to symptoms.

hip_oa.label: Hip osteoarthritis or impingement
hip_oa.notes: Strength and range within comfort; deep hip flexion with rotation often provokes impingement.

hip_replacement.label: Hip replacement
hip_replacement.notes: Follow the surgeon's precautions for the approach used (for a posterior approach: no deep flexion, crossing the midline or inward rotation early on).

shoulder_tendinopathy.label: Shoulder pain: rotator cuff or subacromial
shoulder_tendinopathy.notes: Progressive exercise works; heavy loading isn't clearly better than lighter loading; keep pain tolerable. Landmine and short-range incline pressing are gentler than full overhead work while it settles.

shoulder_instability.label: Shoulder instability or dislocation history
shoulder_instability.notes: Strength through mid-range first; end-range loaded positions last.

wrist_hand.label: Wrist or hand injury, carpal tunnel
wrist_hand.notes: Neutral wrists: push-ups on handles, dumbbells or a bar; forearm planks; carries with straps if grip is limited.

elbow_tendinopathy.label: Tennis or golfer's elbow
elbow_tendinopathy.notes: Slow, progressive wrist and forearm loading; keep heavy grip moderate while it settles.

plantar_fasciitis.label: Plantar fasciitis (heel pain)
plantar_fasciitis.notes: High-load slow calf raises with a towel under the toes (3 s up, 2 s hold, 3 s down, every other day) improved pain faster than stretching. Dose it: first-step pain the next morning shouldn't rise.

achilles.label: Achilles tendinopathy
achilles.notes: Slow, heavy calf loading; reintroduce running and jumping gradually.

hernia.label: Hernia or abdominal separation (diastasis)
hernia.notes: Exhale on effort and avoid hard bracing; follow the surgeon's or physio's guidance after repair.

pregnancy.label: Pregnancy
pregnancy.notes: Moderate resistance and aerobic work are recommended for uncomplicated pregnancies, with the care provider's OK. Avoid contact and fall-risk activities and long periods flat on the back later in pregnancy; avoid overheating.

glaucoma.label: Glaucoma or retinal problems
glaucoma.notes: Head-down positions and breath-holding raise eye pressure.

hypermobility.label: Hypermobility (HSD, hEDS)
hypermobility.notes: Strength through a controlled mid-range; closed-chain and isometric work first; limit passive stretching.

fall_risk.label: Falls or poor balance (often 65+)
fall_risk.notes: Balance plus functional and strength training cut falls by about a third; 3+ hours a week works best. Train balance next to a support, and practise getting up from the floor.

neck.label: Neck pain or cervical problems
neck.notes: Deep-neck-flexor and upper-back work; avoid loading through the head.

diabetes.label: Diabetes or insulin resistance
diabetes.notes: Whole-body resistance training and walking after meals help glucose control. With neuropathy: check the feet, and caution with impact and balance.

mixes.title: Full-body strength
mixes.use: The default 2–3×/week session: one of each big pattern.

mixes.title: Upper body
mixes.use: Upper day of an upper/lower split.

mixes.title: Lower body
mixes.use: Lower day of an upper/lower split.

mixes.title: Anywhere, 20 minutes
mixes.use: Travel, hotel room, no gym: wall, floor, chair, towel, backpack.
mixes.format: Circuit: 3 rounds, 40 s work / 20 s rest.

mixes.title: Back-friendly strength
mixes.use: Disc or chronic low-back problems: neutral spine, trunk endurance.

mixes.title: Blood-pressure-friendly
mixes.use: High blood pressure: no breath-holding, isometric finisher.
mixes.format: Main lifts RPE ≤ 8, 8–15 reps; breathe out on every effort. Finish with 4 × 2 min wall sit or handgrip (Edwards 2023).

mixes.title: Bone builder
mixes.use: Low bone density (with a clinician's OK): heavy-ish weight-bearing lifts and balance.

mixes.title: Strong and steady
mixes.use: Older adults or fall risk: balance + strength, near a support.
mixes.format: Balance work next to a wall or chair; 3+ hours a week of this kind of work cuts falls the most (Sherrington 2019).

mixes.title: Functional and athletic
mixes.use: Real-life strength: carries, crawls, single-leg, rotation, power.

mixes.title: Injury-proofing add-on
mixes.use: Add to any session 1–2×/week, especially for running and field sports.

mixes.title: Warm-up (RAMP)
mixes.use: Before any strength session: raise, activate, mobilise, prime.

mixes.title: Conditioning EMOM
mixes.use: Short, hard conditioning when there's no time for cardio.
mixes.format: Every minute on the minute, 20 min, rotate the four. Not for uncontrolled blood pressure or heart conditions.
